A Ghanaian diplomat born in Kumasi, who was Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1997 to 2006, the first from sub-Saharan Africa.

He had spent his career in the UN and led its peacekeeping department during the failures of Rwanda and Bosnia, which he later admitted. As Secretary-General he set the Millennium Development Goals, pushed the idea that states have a responsibility to protect their people, and opposed the 2003 Iraq war. He and the UN shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2001. Later he mediated after Kenya's 2007 election violence and in Syria. He is buried in Accra. See also Ghana.
sum: A Ghanaian diplomat born in Kumasi, who was Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1997 to 2006, the first from sub-Saharan Africa.
